deck: Week 8, and the Luckbox Index needs a bigger font. Asim won the weekly hundo with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback. Jacoby Brissett scored 3.46. The other eight starters scored 142.4, Asim beat Ivan by 41, and he found out Tuesday morning: "Omg I won the weekly 😭." Arfan, who had posted "gg bro. This make it 500?" on Sunday night assuming the check was his, answered with a broom emoji and the word "Witch." Elsewhere: Bazaan lost Lamar Jackson on the first snap of the game, conceded at 12:36 PM, and won anyway, because Adonai Mitchell scored 23.7 in his flex after six weeks of zeros. Haroon lost to that. Nabil conceded at 3:54 PM, after which Kashir posted the win-probability swing ("8% to 48% Nabil lmaooooo") just to make sure he knew. The commissioner won the lowest-scoring game of the season, 69.98 to 54.08. The Judkins trade flipped. And the entire league spent Halloween afternoon sending the commissioner old photos of each other for the video, which is either community or a hostage situation. (Both. It's both.)

teams.biggestDevelopment: 139.68 with a 116.8-point bench; Burrow 39.48. 7-1, two games clear.

movementReasons.reason: Flowers 0.0, Myers 2.0; Pollard on bye next

teams.headline: THIS MAKE IT 500?
teams.verdict: 139.68, 7-1, and a bench that scored 116.8. Arfan asked Sunday night if the check made it $500. It did not. He's at $200. Asim got this one.
teams.analysis:
Joe Burrow threw for 39.48 points against Tennessee, the second-best quarterback line anyone's had this year behind Josh Allen's 40.82 in Week 2, and Tony Pollard, in the same game on the other sideline, ran for 27.2. Bowers 24.7, Smith-Njigba 20.8, Henry 13.0. Zay Flowers scored 0.0 as a starter in Baltimore's 36-10 loss, Jason Myers kicked 2.0 in his first week replacing Zvada, and the Browns defense added 2.0, and none of it mattered because Arfan scored 139.68 and Yaseen's 119.4 was the fourth-best total of the week and still lost by twenty. The bench scored 116.8. Tyler Allgeier had 33.6 on it. Michael Wilson, playing through broken ribs, had 22.8. Jonah Coleman 18.4, Kincaid 16.6, Dicker 11.0. The bench alone would have beaten seven teams this week. I'm going to say that again next week and it's going to be true again.

The money conversation. Sunday afternoon, Asim: "Plz give me A chance this week @Arfan. How much have you won on weekly's already? $400 😭." Arfan, correcting the record: "200. Pretty sure you won more." (Asim had won zero. Arfan knew that.) Then, with Monday night still to come: "@Asim gg bro. This make it 500?" It did not make it 500. Asim scored 145.86 to Arfan's 139.68 and the check went to Houston's luckiest man, and Tuesday morning Arfan responded to the news the way a man responds when the Nazr finally finds him: a broom emoji, then "Witch." His other contribution to the week was the correct read on the Allen trade, delivered to Asim as an accusation: "you robbed @Haroon with that trade. Put that in the video." Consider it put.

7-1, 65-23 against the field, 987.22 points, and a two-game lead on everyone with six to play. The Luckbox Index is +1.09, which is modest for a team this far ahead, and the formula gives him first by eighteen points, which is not a debate. Eight moves all season. He's at RN Sunday with Pollard on bye, and Mustafa has already filed his pregame: "i need yaseen to give me more of that luck." Yaseen: "Bro, I ran out." Arfan's costume for the Week 7 video, per Asim, was "coming as himself," and the reviews were unanimous: "accurate af." It's the only costume in the league that's 7-1.

teams.headline: THE HUNDO WITH BRISSETT
teams.verdict: 145.86, the weekly high and Asim's first $100, with Jacoby Brissett at quarterback for Purdy's bye. Brissett scored 3.46. Five straight wins, 6-2, second on the board.
teams.analysis:
I want you to sit with the lineup card. Purdy was on bye, so Asim picked up Jacoby Brissett, who is the quarterback Mustafa won with in Week 5 and dropped in Week 6, and Brissett scored 3.46 points. Three point four six. And Asim won the weekly hundo. Bhayshul Tuten ran for 28.9 in the flex in a 42-7 Jaguars win. The Jaguars defense, also new, scored 21.0 in the same game. Bucky Irving 21.0 in a Tampa game where the Bucs won 16-0 without completing a pass. Puka 19.5, Rashee Rice 14.8 in his first game back, Kraft 14.3, and Tyler Bass, picked up for Fairbairn's bye, 16.0. Nine starters, one of them a quarterback scoring like a kicker, and 145.86. The Luckbox Index doesn't have a column for this. I'm adding one.

The week in Asim: Halloween afternoon he announced "I've been waiting for this moment my whole life" when the commissioner asked for old photos of the league for the video, and then spent four hours sourcing them. Sunday he begged Arfan for a chance, got told "Won't work on me witch," watched Arfan post "This make it 500?" at 7:59 PM, and replied "Anyone's game!!! I feel it!" It was, in fact, his game. Tuesday morning: "Omg I won the weekly 😭." Then, to Arfan: "anything is possible!!" Arfan: "🧹. Witch." The Nazr has a new direction and it's pointing at Asim and it has a broom.

The board is the desk's call and it's a big one. The formula ranks Asim fifth: 42-46 against the field, +2.18 on the Index, the luckiest season anyone's had since the spreadsheet was built. The desk ranks him second, because he's 6-2, because the five-game winning streak includes Arfan, Haroon and now the weekly high, because the Allen trade reads +58.28 in his favor and Arfan said "robbed" out loud, and because at some point winning every week has to count for something or the formula is just a points-for column with extra steps. The ceiling moves up to fifth. Sunday he's at RamBam, who just won with 69.98. Asim's doom-post is already loaded; it's just a matter of which day he fires it.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Beat Nabil by 5.96 after Nabil conceded at 3:54 PM; "8% to 48%."

teams.headline: 8% TO 48%
teams.verdict: 119.32 over Nabil by 5.96. Nabil conceded at 3:54 PM. Kashir posted the win-probability chart two hours later. 5-3, third in everything, and the Bengals defense scored 2.0.
teams.analysis:
Kashir won a game he was briefly losing badly, which is the only way Kashir enjoys winning. Braelon Allen 22.3, Jordan Love 21.52, Warren 20.8, McBride 16.7, Aubrey 12.0, Jefferson 11.8. The soft spots were real: St. Brown 9.1, Parker Washington 3.1 in the flex, and the Bengals defense, a one-week rental for the Texans' bye, 2.0 in a game Cincinnati gave up 36. Blake Corum had 13.3 on the bench, Dylan Sampson 9.9. 119.32 beat Nabil's 113.36, and the interesting part was how everyone handled it. Nabil posted "Ggs @Kashir" at 3:54 PM Sunday with the late games still on. At 5:56 PM Kashir posted the ESPN win-probability chart with the caption "8% to 48% Nabil lmaooooo," which is Kashir's way of accepting a concession. Nabil: "Bro, i already said ggs..you good." He was not good. He was never going to be good about it.

Kendrick Bourne is on IR with a high-ankle sprain, which matters mostly because Kashir has made 21 moves and the bench is now Skattebo, Corum, Cooper, Travis Hunter and Sampson, which is a lot of lottery tickets for a 5-3 team that's third in points. He also, for the record, declined to engage with Bilal's worst line of the week, which this site also declines to engage with. Kashir's "Naaaa don't start with me" is the correct response and it's the last word on it here.

The board. 5-3, third in the standings, 55-33 against the field (tied with Bilal), 888.34 points, third, and a Luckbox Index of exactly 0.00, which means Bazaan has handed the title of the league's least lucky and least unlucky man to Kashir. The formula had Bilal second and Kashir third, 0.8 apart. The desk puts Kashir third behind Asim and Bilal fourth, on record. It's close. It'll stay close. Sunday he hosts Naafay, who just scored 54, with Warren on bye and Corum ready. I don't think Kashir is losing that one. I also didn't think he'd need a win-probability chart to beat Nabil.

teams.biggestDevelopment: 125.1; Higgins 32.5 against Mustafa again. Judkins ledger flipped to +1.60.
teams.headline: EVERY TIME WE PLAY, HIGGINS
teams.verdict: 125.1, two straight wins, 4-4, and Tee Higgins' 32.5 against Mustafa, again. Bilal started Dak. Dak outscored Stafford. The Rule may finally be dead.
teams.analysis:
Let's start with the rivalry nobody asked for. Sunday, 3:48 PM, Bilal to Mustafa: "tell me why everytime we play my boi T.Higgins makes it his mission to have the best game 🤣🤣🤣. Gotta love our rivalry!" Higgins caught ten balls for 155 yards and two touchdowns, 32.5 points, in a Bengals game that finished 43-36. Gibbs 23.8, Jacobs 20.2 in his second week back, Dak Prescott 19.8 as the starter with Stafford (8.28, questionable) on the bench, which means the quarterback Bilal started outscored the quarterback he didn't, and the Stafford Rule, after seven weeks of invocation, may have finally been repealed by the simple act of starting the right guy twice in a row. Freiermuth 10.6, Gay 10.0. The holes were Drake London (1.3 in a Falcons game that ended 0-16), Judkins 5.9, and the Seahawks defense 1.0. 125.1 beat Mustafa by 40.

Bilal has changed, and Yaseen noticed. When Yaseen posted "I hope i play you in the playoffs" at Mustafa and then "just know it's win," Bilal's response was "I feel alittle hate in your heart Yaseen… 💔," and Yaseen, stunned, replied "Mannn, Bilal changed. Old Bilal would have took a shot at me." Bilal: "Been changed bro!" The new Bilal also delivered "Damn luckboxes calling out luckboxes! 👀👀👀 you gotta love it" at the Yaseen-Mustafa exchange and asked Yaseen to help Mustafa "get that hate out of his heart." He is now the league's peacemaker, which is a strange career turn for the man who wrote Bilal's Law. He also reopened trade talks with Bazaan Monday ("Who you want for swift! Send me an offer"), with the deadline a week away.

The board moves him up one to fourth, and the formula wanted him second: 55-33 against the field, 906.82 points, second in the league, and a Luckbox Index of −1.00. He's 4-4 and fourth in the standings and the desk keeps him fourth, behind Asim's record and Kashir's. The ceiling holds at three. And the trade tracker has news: Judkins' 5.9 against two bench zeros from Evans and Montgomery, both on bye, flipped the ledger to Team MBK +1.60. Kashir's "two bench players for a starter" verdict is now in the Corrections conversation. Sunday he hosts Nabil with Freiermuth and Dowdle on bye. Nabil concedes early. Bilal should keep playing anyway.

teams.headline: THE DOBBINS LEVEL, THIRD EDITION
teams.verdict: 97.76, a loss to a team that got 0.0 from its quarterback, Tre Tucker at 0.0 in the flex, and Jaylen Waddle's 13.4 on the bench. Three times now. It's his award.
teams.analysis:
Two weeks ago Tre Tucker scored 18.8 on Haroon's bench and it cost him the Asim game. So this week Haroon started him. Tucker scored 0.0. Jaylen Waddle, on the bench, scored 13.4. The margin was 7.54. That's the third Dobbins Level loss for the man who inspired the award (Weeks 5, 7 and 8), and I need to stop pretending anyone else can win it. Here's the rest: Josh Allen 26.56 against Baltimore, Ja'Marr Chase 25.6, Watson 13.3, Kyren 12.4. Aaron Jones 5.0 on the bad knee, Andrews 2.9, Loop 3.0 with an IR tag. 97.76. The opponent was Bazaan, whose quarterback was Lamar Jackson, who got hurt on the first snap and scored 0.0. Haroon lost to a team that started a zero at quarterback. There's no Level for that. I checked.

He didn't say much, which is how you know it hurt. "🥲🥲" at 10:42 PM Monday is the whole post-game. The only other Haroon of the week was clearing up a trade Asim thought he'd made ("Its in the other league. Lol"), which means Haroon is in multiple leagues and losing in the same way in all of them. The Allen ledger reads +58.28 for Asim now, and Arfan put it bluntly in the chat: "you robbed @Haroon with that trade." Haroon did not reply to that either.

The board drops him to fifth, and that's the desk's call, not the formula's. The formula has him fourth: 920.76 points (second in the league), 52-36 against the field (fourth), and a Luckbox Index of −1.73, the unluckiest number the sheet has ever produced. Three weeks ago this team was first on the board at 3-3. It's 3-5 now, eighth in the standings, and the desk can't keep putting a .375 team in the top four on all-play alone. Kittle's back from bye Sunday at Yaseen, who's lost three straight. Somebody's going to feel better Monday morning. The sheet says it's Haroon. The sheet has said that every week since September.

teams.verdict: 113.36, a loss by 5.96, a concession at 3:54 PM Sunday, and Emmett Johnson's 22.8 on the bench. Nabil joins Haroon as a two-time Dobbins Level member.
teams.analysis:
The scoring was fine. Maye 22.46, DeMario Douglas 15.1, Rachaad White 13.0, Chase Brown 12.1, McLaughlin 12.0, the Rams defense 11.0. Walker 10.4 against Denver, Lamb 9.3, Loveland 8.0. 113.36 is the sixth-best score of the week and loses to exactly one of the five teams above it, and Nabil played that one. It's his second Dobbins Level (Week 6, Loveland and Shough), and he's now tied for most appearances with the man the award is named after.

The concession timing stat continues. Week 5: Sunday 11:54 AM. Week 6: Monday 9:29 PM. Week 8: Sunday 3:54 PM, "Ggs @Kashir," with the late games still on and Kashir's win probability, per Kashir, at 48 percent. Kashir posted the chart two hours later to make a point. Nabil: "Bro, i already said ggs..you good." Nabil is now 0-for-3 on concessions that needed to be made, which is a strange record to hold and he holds it alone. He also weighed in on Yaseen's playoff guarantee with "Fr fr no 🧢," which is the first time Nabil has agreed with Yaseen about anything.

3-5 and ninth in the standings, but 44-44 against the field and 859.04 points, fifth, and a Luckbox Index of −1.00. The board holds him at sixth, which is where the formula had him, and the trade ledger on the Lamb deal is down to RamBam +27.70 after a week where Taylor scored 4.7, Emanuel Wilson 0.0, and Johnson 22.8 on the wrong side of Nabil's lineup. If Johnson keeps scoring, that trade's going to get interesting in a way neither manager expected. Sunday he's at Bilal, who's won two straight and has Higgins. Nabil's concession is scheduled for roughly 4 PM.

teams.headline: SIXTY-NINE NINETY-EIGHT
teams.verdict: The lowest winning score of the season, 69.98 to 54.08, with Daniels back, Emanuel Wilson at 0.0 and Jonathan Taylor at 4.7. A win's a win. The board didn't count it as one.
teams.analysis:
Jayden Daniels came back from the bye and scored 14.98 in a Commanders win. Matthew Golden 17.4, the Packers defense (a new pickup) 12.0, Ryan Flournoy 11.6. That's the good news, and it's 56 points. The rest: Emanuel Wilson 0.0 in a Seattle loss, Jonathan Taylor 4.7 in a 42-7 Colts loss to Jacksonville (yes, the same game that gave Asim Tuten's 28.9 and the Jaguars defense's 21.0), Tyler Warren 3.8, Hunter Henry 4.5 on a questionable tag, Shrader 1.0. Rome Odunze had 10.7 on the bench. 69.98 total. And it won, because Naafay scored 54.08, the lowest score anyone's posted this season, and the two of them produced the lowest-scoring game of the season. The chat didn't mention it. The chat was busy with Halloween photos.

Speaking of which, the commissioner's week was spent on the video. Monday night: "asim send me all the crazy photos you got. i have next weeks video on lock." Halloween afternoon: "These pics are insane ngl." The league spent four hours sourcing photos of each other, Mustafa objected to one in particular, Kashir called it "a lesson of doxing all social media," and Asim summed up the project: "it's better to be a surprise for next week." The site has no comment on the photos. The site has a lot of comment on 69.98.

4-4, fifth in the standings on the tiebreak, 39-49 against the field, 798.72 points, ninth, and the Luckbox Index has him at +0.45, which is what a win with 69.98 does to your luck number. The board holds him at seventh, the formula agrees, and the ceiling rank slips from fifth to sixth, because the version of this team with Daniels and Taylor healthy was supposed to be the ceiling and it just scored 70 with both of them playing. The ledger on the Lamb trade is down to +27.70. Sunday he hosts Asim, who's 6-2, won five straight, and is going to tell the chat he's about to lose. He isn't.

teams.biggestDevelopment: 119.4 and a third straight loss, to Arfan. "Bro, I ran out."
teams.headline: I RAN OUT
teams.verdict: 119.4, which beats eight teams this week, and a third straight loss, because the ninth was Arfan. 4-4. Yaseen, asked for luck: "Bro, I ran out."
teams.analysis:
Yaseen scored 119.4, which is a good score, which is the problem. Hubbard 21.4, Trevor Lawrence 19.4 (started over Bryce Young's 10.36 this time, so the Stafford Rule has left Tokyo), Fannin 18.4, the Commanders defense 14.0 in its first week on the roster, Diggs and Garrett Wilson 11.3 each. Jeanty 8.8, McMillan 8.8, Cam Little 6.0. Burden had 15.1 on the bench. 119.4 is the fourth-best total of the week and it lost by twenty because Arfan's bench alone scored 116.8. Three straight losses, from 4-1 to 4-4, and the no-hate theory is now officially a historical document.

The chat exchange of the week belongs to Yaseen and Mustafa, with Bilal refereeing. Mustafa: "i need yaseen to give me more of that luck." Yaseen: "Bro, I ran out." Then: "Also, I've still put up more points then your team lol." (True: 798.06 to 719.58.) Then, at Mustafa: "I hope i play you in the playoffs." Bilal: "I feel alittle hate in your heart Yaseen… 💔." Yaseen: "Nah, just know it's win." It's the most confident anyone's been about a hypothetical December game in October, and I respect it, and he's lost three straight. His other note was about the photo exchange: "It didn't have to be private. Could have sent it a different group with Rameel lol." The league's transparency advocate.

4-4, sixth in the standings, 38-50 against the field, 798.06 points, tenth, and a Luckbox Index of +0.55, down from +1.45 two weeks ago, which is what three losses do. The board holds him at eighth, the formula agrees, and the ceiling stays at eight. The ledger on the Young trade is +36.66 after Adonai Mitchell scored 23.7 for Bazaan this week while Young sat on Yaseen's bench, which is the first time that trade has moved in Bazaan's direction since it was processed. Sunday he hosts Haroon, who's 3-5 and the unluckiest man on record. One of them gets to feel normal on Monday.

teams.headline: RULED OUT, GGS, I'LL SEE YAL NEXT WEEK
teams.verdict: 105.3 and a win over Haroon with Lamar Jackson scoring 0.0 after one snap. Bazaan conceded at 12:36 PM. Adonai Mitchell scored 23.7 in the flex. Nothing about this week is normal.
teams.analysis:
Sunday, 12:21 PM: "Lamar hurt first play can't make this up 😂." Lamar Jackson, back from a three-game absence, hit his throwing hand on a Bills pass rusher on the first offensive snap and was done. 12:36 PM: "Ruled out ggs I'll see yal next week." Bazaan conceded with a zero at quarterback and most of the afternoon still ahead. Then D'Andre Swift ran for 26.9 in Seattle. Then the Buccaneers defense, picked up this week, posted 15.0 in a 16-0 shutout. Then James Cook ran for 17.1 against the team that had just hurt Lamar. Then Chad Ryland, dropped three weeks ago and re-signed since, kicked 10.0. And then, in the flex, Adonai Mitchell, the return for Bryce Young, who had scored 0.0 in every single week since the trade went through, caught 23.7 points against the Raiders. Bazaan won 105.3 to 97.76 with nothing from his quarterback. Kyler Murray scored 19.9 on the bench. (Yes.) Haroon lost to this. I covered it in Haroon's column and I'm still not over it.

The Lamar news is bad. Surgery on the thumb, injured reserve, and his coach says it's possible the season's over; mid-December is the earliest anyone's suggesting. Tyler Huntley got hurt too, so Baltimore's on its third quarterback. For Bazaan that means Kyler is the starter now, which, given the 19.9, is less of a demotion than it sounds. The Bazaan Transaction Rate: 41 moves, four this week (Okonkwo, Buccaneers, Kiner, Ryland back), and Monday morning he opened the shop: "Ajb swift Coker package deal." Bilal and Arfan both asked for the price within three hours. The NFL deadline is next Tuesday. The Kingwood one is whenever Bazaan stops typing.

The board moves him up to ninth over Ivan, which is the desk's call on record: he's 4-4 and seventh in the standings, Ivan is 3-5. The formula had them the other way around by 0.6. 38-50 against the field, 785.48 points, and the Luckbox Index finally moved: +0.55, after seven weeks at exactly zero. The ceiling drops to eleven because Lamar was the ceiling, and he's gone. The Young ledger is Gang Green +36.66, down from +60.36, because Mitchell exists now. Sunday he's at Ivan, who had his whole bench on bye. If Bazaan concedes again before 1 PM, I'm no longer counting it.

teams.headline: THE EMPTY BENCH
teams.verdict: 104.18 and a 41-point loss to Asim with every single bench player on bye or out. Cousins 28.18. The Judkins ledger flipped to Bilal by 1.60. Ivan has not spoken in two weeks.
teams.analysis:
Ivan's bench scored 0.0 this week. Not a bad week on the bench, a literal zero: McCaffrey, Olave, Woody Marks and Vele on the 49ers and Saints bye, Montgomery and Evans on the Texans and 49ers bye, Carnell Tate out. Seven players, no points, and two of them (McCaffrey and Evans) are the reasons he traded Judkins away. The starters did what they could. Kirk Cousins threw for 28.18 in a Raiders win, the Steelers defense 16.0, Jameson Williams 15.0, Hockenson 13.8, Chris Rodriguez, a waiver add, 12.3. Jeremiyah Love started on an IR tag and scored 2.3 before the ankle. Jakobi Meyers 3.4, Goedert 5.2. 104.18 is an average score in an average week. He played the weekly high. He lost by 41.68.

Ivan has now gone two full weeks without a message in the chat, which given the subject matter in that chat is probably wisdom. The silence extends to the trade tracker, where he's been winning the Evans-Montgomery-for-Judkins deal since the day it processed and is now, as of Sunday, losing it: Team MBK +1.60, after Judkins scored 5.9 for Bilal and both of Ivan's guys scored zero on bye. Kashir's "two bench players for a starter" was the chat's consensus for five weeks. It's a 1.6-point lead the other way now, and it'll move again Sunday when Evans and Montgomery are back from bye and Judkins plays again. The point is it moves.

The board. 3-5, tenth in the standings, 38-50 against the field, 821.82 points, and 977.78 points allowed, the most in the league by sixty, which is the Luckbox Index saying he's played the wrong people at the wrong time all year. The formula had him ninth; the desk has him tenth behind Bazaan on record. The ceiling holds at twelve. Sunday he hosts Bazaan with the Steelers defense and Boswell on bye, so the kicker and defense slots are a waiver run he hasn't made yet. McCaffrey, Olave, Vele and Evans all come back. It's a different team. It's still 3-5.

movementReasons.reason: 54.08, the season low; 2-6, four straight losses

teams.headline: FIFTY-FOUR POINT OH EIGHT
teams.verdict: 54.08, the lowest score anyone has posted this season, in a loss to 69.98. Four straight losses, 2-6, and still the seventh-best all-play record in the league. Explain that.
teams.analysis:
I'm going to read the starters and I need you not to look away. Caleb Williams 13.98. The Bears defense 10.0. Bijan Robinson 7.6 in a game Atlanta lost 0-16. Javonte 6.2. Jake Bates 6.0. Pickens 5.8. Jordan Mason 2.0 in the flex. Kyle Pitts 1.6. DK Metcalf 0.9 against Cleveland. 54.08. The previous season low was Bazaan's 61.4 a week ago, and before that Bilal's 66.68 with four backups. Naafay beat them both with his actual starters. Jordan Addison had 10.1 on the bench, Shakir 8.9, Courtland Sutton (a new pickup) 7.3. None of it would have mattered; the margin was 15.9 and the commissioner scored 69.98, which is the lowest winning score of the season and still won by sixteen.

Naafay said nothing. Two straight weeks of nothing, which for a man who posted "I can never beat Haroon mannn" in October is a vow of silence. Asim said it for him, Sunday afternoon, on behalf of a different league: "Why has bijan been ass. I have him in keeper league." Bijan has scored 6.3, 14.7 and 7.6 in the last three weeks for the team whose entire archetype is "The Bijan Build." The build is the problem. The Bears defense, which Naafay dropped for the Jaguars and re-added, scored 10.0, so at least that saga has a positive number in it now.

Here's the stat that keeps this column from being a eulogy: IVaafay is 40-48 against the field, seventh in the league, ahead of RamBam, Yaseen, Ivan and Bazaan, all of whom have more wins. The Luckbox Index is −1.64, second-worst on record behind only Haroon. He's 2-6 with a roster that's scored more than four teams with better records. The board keeps him eleventh on record, the ceiling holds at nine, and the formula, which had him eleventh too, isn't arguing. Sunday he's at Kashir with Metcalf on bye, and Kashir is 5-3 with everyone healthy. I'm not going to predict it. I'm going to note that the last time Naafay was an underdog this big, he scored 54.

teams.biggestDevelopment: Mahomes 25.44 in a 40-point loss; Reichard 0.0. "Only I can call myself a luckbox."
teams.headline: ONLY I CAN CALL MYSELF A LUCKBOX
teams.verdict: 84.74, a loss to Bilal and Tee Higgins, again, and Will Reichard at 0.0. Mahomes scored 25.44 and it didn't matter. 3-5, 22-66 against the field, and a new rule about who's allowed to use the word.
teams.analysis:
The good: Mahomes 25.44 in a loss in Denver, DJ Moore 14.6 in his first week back from the shoulder, Barkley 11.9, Kelce 9.2. Geno Smith, the Jets quarterback, showed up on the bench with 18.0, and McConkey 10.6. The bad: Will Reichard, the Vikings kicker, 0.0, which I didn't know kickers could do in a game their team played. Charbonnet 4.4, Bernard 5.5, the Vikings defense 5.0. 84.74 against Bilal's 125.1, and against Tee Higgins' 32.5 specifically, which prompted the rivalry message from Bilal and a reply from Mustafa about Higgins that the desk is paraphrasing as "unprintable." Bilal, to Yaseen: "please help Mustafa get that hate out of his heart bro!"

Mustafa's great contribution to Kingwood law this week came Sunday afternoon, after Bilal called the Yaseen-Mustafa exchange "luckboxes calling out luckboxes": "Man can't really call me a luckbox with all the injuries I've had. Only I can call myself a luckbox." That's the rule now. Self-identification only. He'd already used it Thursday ("I'm a luckbox," unprompted, before kickoff), so he's in compliance. His other notes: "Where's the party" when the Week 7 video dropped with the Halloween costumes, and a firm objection to one of the photos circulating for the next one, followed by "Still better than the other one." There is always another one.

The board holds him at twelfth, the formula agrees by fourteen points, and nothing on the sheet argues: 3-5, 22-66 against the field, 719.58 points, both the worst in the league by a wide margin, 28 moves, and a Luckbox Index of +1.00, which is what happens when you're 3-5 with the scoring profile of a 1-7 team. The ceiling moves up a spot to ten over Bazaan, because Mahomes just scored 25, Moore is back, Barkley and Smith exist, and Lamar doesn't anymore. Sunday he hosts Arfan with Bernard on bye. Mustafa has already asked Yaseen for luck. Yaseen said he ran out. Arfan said the juju doesn't work on him. That's the whole preview.
